locator.text: Equation (9.5), p. 104, in the statement of Proposition 9.3

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary:
Lean uses a different formula here. The paper's (9.5) is a physical statement: the Cartesian space-time jet norm (5.23) of the flat field F^[j] (base error + pulse-cutoff tails + cutoff remainders, p. 103) is at most C_{j,m,N} q^N for every N, and the next sentence says the bound is uniform over bands, labels and points.

No Lean declaration states this, and the repository defines no physical field for the flat part alone. What it states is flatness in the normalized chart, one theorem per summand of `errors.total = base + gaussian + aliasError`, each for every real α: `baseError_native` (gain h·α, loss 0), `gaussian_field_native` (gain h·α, loss 2·h·m, under hN), `axis_native` with `alias_eq_lift` (gain h·α, loss 0). Each is a bound A·Q_n^(h·α − loss m)·S_n^p on chart derivatives of order ≤ m for bands n ≥ 4, and each is a `NativeBounds` on the OPEN strip domain (or its lift); `NativeBounds.smooth` and `.bounds` say nothing off that open set. The hypotheses are met by the construction (`state_invariant`).

Where the display does follow by formal steps: at physical points whose profile radius is strictly inside the active interval. There the chart point lies in the open lifted strip (`movingStrip_domain` is an iff with Ioo; the strict radius bound is algebra from the stated squared-radius identity), so `native_lift`, `NativeBounds.weaken`, `excluded_nativeBounds` give one bound for `errors.total` at any α (exactly lines 861-872 of `native_residual` with α in place of 1/2+σ), `SmoothNear.of_open` gives the smoothness hypothesis, `cartesianPull_jet_bound` (stated for an arbitrary chart field) converts to C·q^(gain − loss) with the S_n^e factor absorbed, and taking α large is exponent arithmetic.

Where it does not: at the two radial endpoints of the active shell. `active` is defined with a closed interval Icc, and `actual_selectedGeometry` puts the chart image of a shell point only in `nativeDomain` and in the closure of the lifted strip (`selected_polar_closure`), never in the open strip. At such a point `cartesianPull_jet_bound` needs `SmoothNear (errors.total n)` at the chart point and the jet bound there; the repository's tool for the latter, `jet_bound_at_closure`, needs `ContDiffAt ℝ ∞` at the edge point. The repository states that smoothness across the edge only for the full residual (`realization_native_smooth`) and uses it only there (`selected_residual_jet_bound`, lines 939-945). For the flat part I found none: `axisFlat`/`gaussianFlat` are classes on `G.strip`, the invariant's `phase` is smooth on `G.strip.domain` only, `fullResidual_decomposition` holds only on the open lifted strip (so smoothness of `errors.total` cannot be read off the full residual), and a search of decls.jsonl signatures and of the sources for ContDiff/smooth statements about `axisymmetricAlias`, the alias states, `errors.gaussian`, `errors.aliasError` or `errors.total` returned nothing. (Gaussian coefficients are smooth on the larger `G.domain` by `gaussianCoefficientSmooth`, but nothing comparable is stated for the alias.) Regularity is an analytic fact under the decision rule, so the display as written (all points) is not a formal consequence.

In the other direction the Lean statements do not follow from the display either: they are per summand and in chart scales, which a physical bound on the sum does not give. So the two are not comparable, and the Lean reaches the surrounding result by another route: it never forms a physical flat bound, but folds the flat terms into the full residual at the fixed gain h·(1/2+σ) and converts only the full residual to physical form, edges included (`residual_jetRate`).

Smaller points: the Lean bounds are for bands n ≥ 4 (q below a fixed scale), and outside the active shell only the base error has a stated physical all-power bound (`base_exterior_jetRate`).

Severity low: the paper uses (9.5) once later, to supply E_{j,m} in (9.18) (p. 114); the Lean obtains the corresponding full-residual rate without a separate flat term.

Not verified: that no smoothness statement for the stage-j alias near the edge exists under a name or shape my searches missed; the index line of `native_residual` is 845 (861 is the cited step).
